content.comment_body: Hello, Recently, I needed to update the IP addresses of some [product_name] devices connected via LAN due to a network change and a new IP range. After assigning new IP addresses, the connections set up in the software between these devices stopped working. Since there were only a few affected, I manually reassigned them in the [product_name] properties and restored operation. For larger projects, I’d like to learn the best way to change a [product_name]'s IP address on a network without losing connections (if possible). Anyone with relevant experience?
When communication occurs between two [product_name] devices, changing their IP addresses on the network will always result in connection issues.

Hello [user_name], Thanks, I've encountered this myself. What’s unclear to me: If I update the IPs of two [product_name] devices within the network project view, the software recognizes their updated addresses, but doesn’t automatically adjust their program connections? Does this mean manual configuration of all network I/O is required whenever IP addresses change?
Could you upload the programs from the two communicating [product_name] devices? If you prefer not to share them publicly, feel free to send them to me in a private message.
Hello [user_name], I've sent you a private message. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that after changing IP addresses of [product_name] devices within a network, communication links break and have to be manually reconfigured within the software. Automatic updating of network I/O connections does not occur, making the process more difficult and prone to errors as projects grow larger.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to intelligently update or preserve network connections after changing IP addresses of [product_name] devices, so manual reconfiguration is no longer necessary.
